findings.title: Default `queued` is evaluated once at import time
findings.body: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated when the class is defined, so every AssignmentSource built without an explicit value gets the same process-start timestamp. The field is meant to record when the assignment was queued, so the value is wrong and misleading. Use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`.

findings.title: to_dict leaves a datetime that may not survive task serialization
findings.body: `asdict` returns `queued` as a datetime object. It is passed in the kwargs of `apply_async`, and Celery with a JSON serializer cannot handle a raw datetime. This can fail at enqueue time or arrive as a string. `from_dict` does `cls(**input_dict)` and would then accept a string `queued` without validation. Serialize `queued` to ISO format and parse it back in `from_dict`.

findings.title: assignment_source kwarg passed to all sync_assignee_outbound implementations
findings.body: The task now always calls `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=...)`. The abstract signature accepts `**kwargs`, but the diff only changes `sync_status_outbound`, and the concrete integrations (Jira, GitHub, etc.) are not updated or checked. Any implementation without `**kwargs` will raise a TypeError on every outbound assignee sync.

findings.title: where_should_sync does not use the assignment source
findings.body: `where_should_sync` calls `should_sync(key)` without a source, so the new cycle check does not apply there. That is acceptable for inbound sync, but the source filtering exists only on the task path, so the protection is incomplete if other outbound paths call `should_sync`.
